text:
Yes. Hansen GFC (version GFC-2025-v1.13) mapped about 81.3 ha of tree-cover loss in 2021 within the property. That is roughly 2.23% of its 3,643.5 ha. The evidence supports this finding: later years were observed (through 2025), and the JRC 2020 forest reference agrees on 98% of the event area.

Context from the MGAP 2021 forest map: 68.1 ha of the loss is planted forest (Pinus elliottii and Pinus taeda), 13.2 ha is outside mapped forest, and none is native forest. Separately, Hansen recorded another 37.3 ha of loss in patches under 0.5 ha, which is not counted in the 81.3 ha.

Limits: this does not show that deforestation or land-use change occurred, since Hansen loss includes plantation harvest. It also does not establish the cause, legality, or responsible party, and it is not a compliance finding (e.g., EUDR).
